title: C# Memory Leak when using Image.CreateFromData with a long-running byte buffer
body:
### Tested versions

Reproducible on Godot 4.5 Beta 3 and 4.4.1 

### System information

Godot v4.5.beta3.mono - Windows 10 (build 19045) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4080 SUPER (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.7602) - AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D 8-Core Processor (16 threads) - 63.62 GiB memory

### Issue description

Okay this is one of the weirder bugs I've seen in a hot minute, but is 100% reproduction rate.

Calling Image.CreateFromData(), with a Byte buffer that is kept in Memory after the call (Ex. a field or property of an object) will cause it to leak a significant amount of memory with every call.  However, if the same function is called using a short-lived clone of the same byte array/a byte array that is not kept in scope, the memory will be properly cleaned up.

Not quite sure how the reference chain is working to result in that behavior, but it's apparently a thing.  At least it's easy to work around (if inefficient) by cloning the byte array before calling.

### Steps to reproduce


1. See MRP
2. Run MRP - Observe climbing memory usage that will scale until you run out of RAM.
3. In the main script file (Script.cs), change the constant at the top of the file, "_ENABLE_BUG" to false.  This will instead call the image function with a .Clone()'d version of the byte array.
4.  Run MRP - Observe memory usage is correct/does not infinitely climb.

> [!WARNING]
> :: PHOTOSENSITIVE WARNING :: The MRP writes random color data to the texture on screen every 0.1s.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[image-memory-leak-mrp.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/21333359/image-memory-leak-mrp.zip)
